title: Design a school library service
summary: Plan book search, borrowing, and returns for a small library. Follow one safe loan and explain what happens when two readers want the same copy.
introduction: Let us put the building blocks together. We will plan a small library service where readers find books and staff track loans. The plan starts small and protects one important rule: a copy cannot be lent to two people at once.
learningObjectives: Turn library needs into a small data model
Trace a loan that saves related changes together
Explain retries, busy periods, and a safe first design

blocks.text: Write the goal and the size

For this design, assume one school, 500 readers, 2,000 book titles, and 5,000 physical copies. Readers search titles; permitted users borrow and return copies. Book sales and payments are outside this plan.

A sample speed goal is that 95 out of 100 searches finish within one second while 10 searches arrive each second. This is a target to test, not a result we have measured. The safety goal is that one copy has at most one current loan.
Name the facts and their owners

rows: Each physical copy has its own identity.
A loan records who has one copy and whether it was returned.
A repeated borrow request can return its saved result.

blocks.text: Use a database suited to linked records and transactions. A **transaction** saves related changes together or saves none. Begin with one application and one database; this size alone does not justify many services.

blocks.alt: The browser asks to borrow copy C7. The service checks permission, saves the loan in one transaction, and returns the result.
blocks.caption: Two people may ask for the same copy. The final availability check and loan update belong in one safe database operation.

blocks.code:
School library: one small service and one database
GET /books?title=moon -> matching public book details
POST /loans {copyId, requestId} -> saved loan or clear refusal
POST /loans/{loanId}/return -> returned loan or already returned

Borrow one copy
1. Check the reader and their permission to borrow.
2. Begin a transaction and claim the unique reader/requestId.
3. For an already saved request, check the details and return its result.
4. For a new request, change Copy.state to on-loan only if still available.
5. If a copy changed, add the Loan; otherwise prepare a refusal.
6. Save that outcome for this requestId and commit together, then reply.
7. Concurrent requests with the same ID wait or retry; do not execute twice.

Rule: a physical copy has at most one current loan.
Reminder failure must not undo a saved loan.
blocks.title: Worked design plan
blocks.caption: Read this as a design plan. It is not a running server or an API you can call.

blocks.text: Follow a search and a borrow

items: A browser sends a title search. The service checks the input and uses an index or search tool that matches the chosen search rules.
The reply lists public book details and copies. A cached availability count is only a hint; it may be old by the time someone chooses a copy.
The borrow request checks the current copy state in the database transaction. If two readers ask together, only one may change the same available copy.
Save the loan and request result with that change. Reply after the commit, which is the point when the transaction is saved.
A return changes the loan and copy together too. Returning an already returned loan should not create another side effect.

blocks.text: The database may save a loan just before the network reply is lost. A reader then retries. Use the same request ID and return the saved result instead of creating another loan. Claim the reader-and-request ID safely so concurrent repeats cannot both run. Check that the same ID is not reused for a different copy.

If saving fails, roll back all related changes. Do not leave the copy marked on-loan without a loan record. Keep a durable record of reminder work if reminders must survive a restart; reminder delays should not block borrowing.

Index common lookups such as book title, copy ID, and current loans for a reader. If public title searches become busy, cache those results. Always use the authoritative loan data for a borrow decision.

If search work begins to slow writes, a separate search index may help. It can be slightly behind, so show that availability is confirmed when borrowing. Monitor errors, slow requests, and conflicting borrow attempts. Practise a restore from backup.

items: A cached page says copy C7 is available. The database now says it is on-loan. What should the borrow request do?
Refuse the new loan clearly and refresh the availability shown. The old page must not override the saved loan rule.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not read "available" and then save a loan as two unprotected steps. Another request can change the copy between those steps.
